correctness.rationale: Binary-sextic sections are enumerated as all 1093 normalized nonzero projective coefficient vectors. Geometric reducedness is exactly degree(f)>=5 and gcd(f,fprime)=1, including root at infinity; 648 forms pass. Every one of the Gaussian binomial 99,463 two-dimensional subspaces is counted once using unique RREF bases, and all four rational members are tested. The 24 projective substitutions enumerate all PGL2 transformations and partition the 10,005 all-smooth pencils into 440 orbits. The 440-entry catalogue and the rational-root/common-divisor histograms are exhaustive outputs. Independent SymPy RREF and 3-generator orbit calculations reproduce every aggregate, so the proof is finite exhaustive rather than a sampled experiment. The elementary projective-plane obstruction follows from two linear jet conditions; no general-degree formula is claimed.

originality.rationale: The new statement is an exact enumeration and PGL2 classification of 2-dimensional subspaces of the binary-sextic section space with all four rational divisors reduced. The closest inspected finite-field smooth-pencil paper gives general existence and different examples, while the inspected genus-two moduli paper counts individual curve strata. Neither statement, nor a formal implication from it, gives this projective-line-in-discriminant-complement count or the 440 source-group orbits. Public mathematical search and research-record comparisons found no equivalent statement; an unindexed census or stronger counting theorem remains a significant priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Worldwide publication priority is not certified: an unindexed complete F3 sextic pencil census may exist.
A stronger general formula for lines avoiding a binary-form discriminant, if known, could imply the exact numerical distribution.
Entin full text was not inspected, although its advertised q->infinity scope does not state this exact small-field result.

value.rationale: An exact finite-field Hurwitz/Bertini invariant is determined at the smallest odd field for genus-two hyperelliptic branch divisors, motivated by Asgarli–Ghioca smooth-pencil existence questions. The complete 10,005-pencil census, 440 source-group orbit representatives and common-branch/splitting profiles give genuinely family-level geometric data; in particular the 9,612 base-point-free pencils realize separable degree-six maps with four reduced rational fibres. These finer distributions are not implied by the number of smooth forms or by the classification of isolated genus-two curves. The trivial no-net jet observation is contextual and not relied on for value.
